To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the major genetic predisposition to PAH is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the bone morphogenetic receptor 2 (BMRP2).

(1) BMPR2 mutations are responsible for most familial and some sporadic cases of PAH; (2) ACVRL1 mutations are associated with PAH in hereditary hemorrhagic teleangiectasia; (3) mutations in other genes have been described in a few cases of PAH, but these are rare; (4) common genetic variants have been identified by genome-wide studies in PAH; (5) genetic diagnosis is available for PAH and is useful for genetic counseling

(a) the major predisposing genes for hereditary predisposition are the BMPR2 gene and the ACVRL1 gene, and (b) the major common genetic predisposing factor for sporadic PAH is a variant in the BMPR2 promoter.
